claim: Google defines toil as manual, repetitive, automatable, reactive work that scales linearly — capped at 50% of SRE time
quote: Toil encompasses the repetitive, predictable, constant stream of tasks related to maintaining a service. Google limits the time SRE teams spend on operational work at 50%.

claim: Google's quarterly SRE surveys show an average actual toil of ~33%, with outliers from 0% to 80%
quote: Quarterly surveys of Google's SREs show that the average time spent toiling is about 33%, so we do much better than our overall target of 50%.

claim: Average team toil rose to ~30% in 2026, up from ~25% in 2024
quote: Operational toil is on the rise again—up to 30% from 25% in 2024, according to recent SRE data.

claim: Toil rose 30% in 2026 — the first increase in five years — despite AI operations tooling adoption
quote: Toil rose 30%, the first increase in five years, despite widespread adoption of AI operations tooling.

claim: Google SRE recommends no more than 2–3 actionable incidents per on-call shift as a sustainable baseline
quote: The Google SRE Workbook recommends no more than 2-3 actionable incidents per shift as a sustainable baseline.

claim: Healthy on-call practices: primary + secondary per shift, follow-the-sun for global coverage, quarterly alert audits
quote: Every production on-call rotation should have a primary and a secondary on-call engineer for each shift.

claim: 2026 DORA MTTR benchmarks: elite <1 hour, high <1 day, medium <1 day, low 1 day–1 week
quote: MTTR: Elite < 1 hour, High < 1 day, Medium < 1 day, Low 1 day – 1 week.

claim: Self-hosted infrastructure requires security patches, OS upgrades, hardware failure management, and performance monitoring — without automation these can consume most engineering time
quote: Maintenance is a real challenge requiring security patches, OS upgrades, hardware failure management, and performance monitoring. Without strong automation, these tasks can consume most engineering time.

claim: The 3-2-1-1-0 rule adds one immutable copy and zero-error verified restores to the classic 3-2-1 rule; only 58% of organizations use immutable storage across all data
quote: At least one copy to be immutable, meaning it cannot be modified or deleted. Zero Recovery Errors: Verified backups tested in isolated sandboxes before crisis situations. Only 58% of organizations use immutable storage across all data.

claim: The 3-2-1 backup rule evolved to 3-2-1-1-0 specifically to address ransomware threats and the need for verified recoveries
quote: Many IT providers and security teams have expanded the traditional model into a more modern framework: 3-2-1-1-0, adding one immutable copy and verified backups with zero errors.

claim: 62% of organizations fail to do regular backup and restoration exercises; 71% do no failover testing at all
quote: A shocking 62% of organizations fail to do regular system backups and restoration exercises. 71% of organizations do no failover testing to ensure their outage prevention protocols are working.

claim: DR testing should occur on a tiered cadence: monthly granular restores, quarterly full recovery tests for critical systems
quote: Every disaster recovery plan should be fully tested at least once per year, with critical Tier 1 systems tested quarterly.

claim: Best-practice cadence: monthly granular restores for critical systems, quarterly full DR exercises, ad-hoc after major changes
quote: Businesses should test basic backup restores monthly, critical systems quarterly, and full disaster recovery procedures annually.

claim: 63% of organizations risk reintroducing dormant malware during restoration because they skip validation steps
quote: 63% of organizations risk reintroducing infections during restoration because they skip critical validation steps.

claim: Kopia offers faster parallel uploads, built-in web UI, and centralized repository server; recommended for multi-machine self-hosted setups
quote: Kopia for most self-hosters because it offers a built-in web interface, faster snapshots, and refined retention policies.

claim: Restic has the broadest cloud backend support, largest community (~34k GitHub stars), and best third-party tool ecosystem
quote: Restic is the best choice for most people — broad cloud backend support, strong deduplication, and the largest community.

claim: pgBackRest is unmaintained as of April 2026; existing installations work but receive no new bug fixes or security updates
quote: pgBackRest is now unmaintained. Maintainer David Steele has stopped work on the project. The tool still functions, but there will be no new updates or bug fixes.

claim: Barman (EDB-backed, actively maintained) is the recommended pgBackRest replacement for on-premises PostgreSQL deployments
quote: If you're starting fresh, go with Barman. It has the strongest corporate backing (EDB is the largest dedicated PostgreSQL company), the most active development, and the smoothest cloud integration story.

claim: WAL-G is recommended for cloud/object storage and Kubernetes PostgreSQL environments in 2026
quote: WAL-G: Originally a Yandex project, written in Go, designed around object storage from day one. Does well with parallel backup and restore, both genuinely fast.

claim: Velero backs up Kubernetes cluster state and persistent volumes as GitOps-native CRDs, enabling version-controlled backup policies
quote: Velero's architecture, built on Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions, enables a fully declarative, GitOps-aligned backup strategy where Backups, Schedules, and Restores are defined as native Kubernetes objects.

claim: Runbook automation reduces MTTR by ~37% (Favor case study); typical P1 MTTR is 45–60 min with 12 min of coordination overhead
quote: Favor achieved a 37% MTTR reduction after adopting incident.io. Typical P1 MTTR ranges from 45-60 minutes without automation, with approximately 12 minutes consumed by coordination overhead alone.

claim: PagerDuty Process Automation provides AI-suggested runbooks from past incident history with enterprise RBAC for production-impacting decisions
quote: PagerDuty Runbook Automation is a SaaS-based environment for authoring, managing and executing automated workflows. Resolve tasks up to 99% faster.
